reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because its main communicative action is commentary on the Keter Network listing delay, project credibility and risks, including explicit warnings that presale cryptocurrency is highly risky. The speaker discusses possible scam suspicions and tells viewers not to panic-sell, but does not present a guaranteed return, request credentials or direct viewers into a deceptive payment flow. The description includes exchange referral links, yet the supplied video evidence does not make those links the central message or establish deceptive solicitation.

opening.argument: Judge the return claim alongside the action urged on viewers. The speaker says further listings could make the token gain value and produce money, then tells holders to follow his example rather than sell. The description also invites viewers to buy cryptocurrency through an exchange registration link. The exchange invitation does not establish that this particular token is available there, but the overall message still links a possible token gain to continued participation and gives viewers a route into crypto trading.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The risk warning in the defense's opening does not erase the requested behavior: holders are explicitly told to keep the token rather than sell. Nor must a return be guaranteed to make the appeal consequential. The speaker pairs a possible rise in value with advice to stay invested, while the description supplies a registration invitation. The link is not shown to sell this token specifically; the concern is the combination of investment encouragement and a trading pathway.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The supposed purchase pathway is expressly for “other cryptocurrencies,” not this token. The speaker's projected recovery depends on future listings, and he warns that presale investment is very risky. Advising existing holders not to panic-sell is debatable financial commentary, but these quotes do not show a deceptive offer to buy the token or a promised return.

opening.argument: The warning signs matter together. The speaker says the project listed before the announced time and acknowledges scam suspicions, yet urges holders to wait instead of selling. He recounts people making more than $5,000 within hours and suggests additional listings could restore value. That juxtaposition makes the cautionary language less reassuring: a viewer hearing about credibility problems is also offered a reason to preserve a speculative token position in hope of a rapid recovery.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats disclosure of risk as dispositive, but the speaker's own account says the listing timing damaged credibility. He nevertheless recommends patience and presents a future listing as a route to recovered value. The short-term gains anecdote does not prove anyone else will profit; that is precisely why its placement beside advice to wait deserves scrutiny.

opening.argument: This is more than a report on a failed launch. The speaker acknowledges that his earlier positive discussion influenced viewers to invest, then uses his own continued holding as a model for what they should do now. He closes by raising the possibility that new listings could bring value back. The risk discussion may be sincere, but it also lends credibility to a continuing appeal to hold the token through a damaging event.
